QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_17

question.text: Mr. Vikram Desai's 'Sahyadri Category II AIF' typically negotiates board seats on investee-company boards. Per the workbook, the number of board seats allotted to an investor should be:

answer.text: Fixed at one seat per investor regardless of ticket size
Allotted on a PRO-RATA basis based on the amount of investment made
Equal for all investors to ensure fairness

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 233-234), board seats on an investee company should be allotted on a pro-rata basis based on the amount of investment made. Where investors come in through a syndicate, the lead investor typically takes the board seat on behalf of the group. The agreement to a board seat alone does not complete the appointment - the appointment must be effected through the company's normal board-appointment mechanics and may require approval of other investors. The Trap: A fixed one-seat-per-investor rule ignores pro-rata economics. 'Equal for all investors' is not the source rule. 'Only SEBI-registered intermediaries' is invented. Note: Funds often reserve the right to a board seat without immediately exercising it - this is a source-supported litigation-risk reservation, preserving negotiation leverage while keeping the fund out of the formal director chair until needed.
